messages:
anya: ran a 12h sim this morning for the 'surprise-holiday-promo' pattern (sudden 4x qps for 3h, then 2x sustained). wanted to surface a few things before we finalize the runbook.
matt: thanks — quick TL;DR? can we absorb without extra reserved capacity?
anya: TL;DR: we can keep latency SLOs if we prewarm 30% more gpus in us-east-1 + enable regional fallback for embeddings to eu-west for 75% of requests. cost delta ~ +$14k/day for the 3h peak if we reserve, ~ +$5k/day if we rely on on-demand + aggressive routing.
kevin: where are the bottlenecks? is it GPU hours or network egress/KV cache misses?
anya: mostly GPU contention on long-context chat models (>=2048 tokens) + KV cache miss rate spikes when cold start a new user cohort. network added ~10-15ms p50 on cross-region failover but wasn't the primary cost.
raul: do you have the numbers from the sim? share the command you ran so we can repro.
anya: pasted the runner here:```bash
# local sim script
python infra_sim.py --pattern "surprise_promo" --qps-mult 4 --duration 10800 --models gpt-like-16k --seed 42 --prewarm 0.3 > run-196321.log
```
matt: nice. what were the key metrics in run-196321.log?
anya: key excerpts: "gpu_hours: 2,740", "peak_concurrent_gpus: 512", "95th_token_latency: 1.2s (baseline 0.45s)", "batching_efficiency: 0.68 -> drops to 0.54 during ramp".
kevin: 2,740 gpu_hours for a 12h sim seems high — is that cluster-aggregated?
anya: yes aggregate across all zones. per-hour avg ~228 GPU-hours/hour during peak window. this maps to ~480 active GPUs with average utilization 47% due to many small convs and cold KVs.
opsbot: [alert] capacity-sim: run-196321 completed; anomaly: KV cache miss spike at t=01:14:55 (~29% miss rate).
sre-oncall: flagged. is the miss spike tied to rollout or traffic skew?
anya: traced to a skewed bucket: 18% of requests hit new prompt_template X that bypasses prefix cache (weird). fixing template => miss rate drops to 8% and 95p latency improves to ~0.9s.
raul: good find. action items?
anya: proposed mitigations: 1) prewarm +30% in us-east-1 starting T-3h; 2) enable embeddings reroute rule: non-low-latency embedding requests -> eu-west cached tier (approx 20% of embedding QPS); 3) temporarily relax batching latency cap from 40ms -> 80ms during ramp to improve batching efficiency; 4) rollout hotfix to prompt_template to restore prefix cache.
matt: cost tradeoffs? pick one recommended plan.
anya: recommended plan = (1) + (3) + (4). that keeps extra cost ~+$5k/day and reduces 95p latency to ~0.75s during peak. full reserved capacity gives best latencies but cost +$14k/day.
kevin: can we do a canary for the reroute rule? we should roll to 10% traffic to eu-west first.
anya: yes — canary config:```yaml
- route: embeddings
  condition: country != US
  percent: 10
```
matt: timeline to ship hotfix for the template?
anya: hotfix PR ready, small change. if we cut it now and patch the next deploy window (T+30m) we get improved cache in ~45m.
raul: who's oncall to approve prewarm?
sre-oncall: I'm here. approve prewarm +30% for window 15:00-18:00 UTC. I'll monitor.
opsbot: [runbook] started prewarm job: prewarm/196321 -> target +153 GPUs in us-east-1 at 15:00 UTC.
matt: add cost tag to the prewarm job and set alert if cost burn > $8k within first hour.
anya: added tags and alert. I'll post a short exec summary after the window with final numbers and recommendations for calendarized reserved buys.
kevin: also capture model-level breakdown (chat vs embeddings) — we need that to recommend quantization/packing for next sprint.
anya: will do. final note: if we see cross-region failover >5% for more than 10m, we switch to fallback variant (small-quantized) automatically. that's baked into the policy.
matt: perfect. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
